html:
South Sudan became independent from Sudan on 9 July 2011, after a referendum in January 2011 in which almost 99 percent of voters chose to separate.

The vote was promised in the Comprehensive Peace Agreement of 2005. Celebrations in Juba marked the end of a struggle that had cost millions of lives in two civil wars. Salva Kiir, who succeeded John Garang, became president.

The new state had most of the old Sudan's oil but no outlet except pipelines through the north, and quarrels over oil fees and the border region of Abyei soon followed. Little over two years later it fell into its own civil war.
sum: South Sudan became independent from Sudan on 9 July 2011, after a referendum in January 2011 in which almost 99 percent of voters chose to separate.
